key_insight: Lipid profiles including ApoB predicted first heart failure events, with lower LDL emerging as the strongest counterintuitive predictor.
clinical_relevance: Routine lipid measurements may offer sex-specific signals of future heart failure, but these associations do not establish causality or justify changing cholesterol treatment.
method: Retrospective analysis of age-matched, multicenter All of Us electronic health records.
Machine learning using lipid panels plus ApoB to predict first heart failure across pre-diagnosis windows.
SHAP analysis to interpret lipid contributions and sex-specific patterns.
evidence_signal: Up to 36 months before first heart failure, AUC was 0.624 in men and 0.627 in women; comparison with age-matched people never diagnosed with cardiovascular disease yielded AUCs of 0.937 and 0.925, respectively.
watch_item: Performance depended strongly on the comparison group, so the high AUCs against cardiovascular-disease-free controls should not be interpreted as equivalent to prospective clinical prediction.
paper_title: Cholesterol Paradox: Multi-point Heart Failure Prediction from Lipid Panels in Electronic Health Records
